evidence.title: Scion
evidence.description:
John Wick meets Ghost in the Shell in this fast-paced cyberpunk thriller by the #1 New York Times bestselling author of The Will of the Many and The Strength of the Few.
My job, when you think about it, isn't so different from a lot of people's.

The more old-fashioned crowd do still get hung up on the "killing people" part of it, I guess, but that's a them problem: it's been perfectly legal to take out lifers for ages. Besides, once ultrawealthy morons realised they had a way to live forever—limited resources be damned—there was only ever going to be one genuinely practical deterrent.

So, sure, I have to deal with a ton of boring planning. Inconvenient hours. Some pretty awkward face-to-face interactions. And like most of us, I'm really only clocking in to try to crawl out from beneath my debts. But someone's got to do it.

Luckily, my genetic compatibilities make me really, really good at doing...

truth_claims.note: conf=0.72; Scion (2026), James Islington's first sci-fi/cyberpunk novel, published Sept 1 2026 (Saga Press US, ISBN 9781668239261 for the ebook; 9781668239247 hardcover). Confirmed as the FIRST book in a new planned series: the author's own announcement says "It's now the first in a planned series," and Text Publishing lists it as "Book 1 in an electrifying new series." The series has no separately announced name yet, so it is being tracked under the title of the first book ("Scion" series, #1) — the series-name portion is inferred from the title; the "book 1 of a series" status itself is publisher-confirmed. Distinct from Islington's Hierarchy series and Licanius Trilogy.

Author confirmed as James Islington. Series is genuinely null: Scion is a standalone cyberpunk thriller, explicitly described by the author as a side project written between edits on the Hierarchy series, and it is not part of Hierarchy or the Licanius Trilogy. No retailer, publisher, or Locus listing assigns it a series name or number; reviewers discuss it as self-contained with only speculation about possible sequels.
